Q1
What does the error `machine constraint violation` mean, and what should I do about it?
constraints are set on a machine whose recorded cloud instance has a different architecture from the one required
only architecture is compared
require the architecture the machine has, or request a new machine
Q2
Reprovisioning a machine fails with `machine agent is still present`. Why, and what should I do?
the machine agent still reports presence
stop the agent or confirm the machine is lost
Q3
Can a controller machine or a container be reprovisioned?
no: a controller machine or a container is not eligible (errors `machine is a controller machine`, `machine is a container`)
only an alive, provider-provisioned machine that hosts no containers qualifies
Q4
Under what conditions does a machine become dead?
only when it is dying
and hosts no containers, units or storage
Q5
What does the error `machine not provisioned` mean?
an action that needs the cloud instance ran before the cloud reported an instance ID
wait until the compute provisioner has recorded the instance
Q6
Which container types can I name in a machine designation in Juju 4.1?
only lxd
another type fails with `invalid container type`
Q7
What does the machine designation `0/lxd/4` refer to?
the existing LXD container 4 on machine 0
Q8
How many levels deep can containers be nested, and what happens if I go deeper?
one level
a deeper name is refused with `machine name "<name>" has too many containers`
Q9
What drives the compute provisioner, i.e. what triggers it to provision machines?
the model machines change stream / watcher
it monitors unprovisioned machines
I remove a machine that still hosts units. What happens, and which error might I see?
the machine is marked dying
it does not become dead while it still hosts units
`machine has units`: remove or move the units first
What does the error `grandparent machine are not supported currently` mean?
the reboot logic found a machine whose parent itself has a parent
name validation refuses containers nested deeper than one level, so it guards an unsupported layout
no remediation
Which record holds a machine's hardware details (CPU, memory, root disk), and what else does it hold?
the cloud instance record
also arch, virtualisation type, availability zone and the creation state (instance id empty until the cloud reports it)
Who writes a machine's status?
the machine agent reports the health status (pending, started, stopped, error)
the controller and the providers/container broker write the provisioning status (allocating, running, provisioning error)
What happens to relation settings of the units on a machine that is reprovisioned?
the units depart their relation scopes
their settings are archived so the remaining units see a consistent departure

removal, status, storage provisioning, network, model migration, recovery and agent passwords (not in the layered page: score separately)
